normative_action: The code-reviewer subagent performs an independent read-only review and does not edit files; Write, Edit and NotebookEdit are disallowed tools.
trigger_scope: code-reviewer subagent (PR, diff, pre-merge or second-pass review)
exceptions: MultiEdit and Bash are not tool-disallowed; the no-edit duty for them rests on the instruction text.

normative_action: The code-reviewer reads the code-review skill first and follows it as the canonical procedure (scope, priorities, owner reads, findings format) without redefining review criteria.
As a subagent the reviewer reads CLAUDE.md and the rule files the code-review procedure names for the changed area instead of assuming they were loaded.
The reviewer returns findings in the code-review output format, including the important areas that could not be verified.

Do not bypass incompatible peer dependencies with npm/pnpm/yarn --force, -f or --legacy-peer-deps (also via npm_config_force / npm_config_legacy_peer_deps environment assignments); resolve the conflict as add-dependency describes. The PreToolUse hook blocks such commands.
modality: MUST NOT (PreToolUse block before execution, fails closed)
trigger_scope: Bash and PowerShell package-manager commands, including wrapped shells up to depth 3
exceptions: If the user explicitly decides to override, the user runs the command.

normative_action: Every added, changed or removed package, and every recognized dependency command, goes through add-dependency: its version selection, deprecation, vulnerability and license steps must have been completed.
modality: MUST (PostToolUse feedback after dependency commands, manifest changes and manifest edits)
trigger_scope: NuGet and npm manifests and package commands in the active worktree
exceptions: Feedback arrives after the change ran; outside Git only a recognized dependency command triggers a full scan.

normative_action: Reserved decisions need explicit approval before implementation: changing an accepted project or architecture decision; adopting a new architectural style or pattern (CQRS, mediator, Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, microservices, Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns); adding a production project/layer/assembly; changing persistence boundaries (incl. multiple persistence contexts) or persistence technology; adding an infrastructure category (messaging, background processing, distributed cache, search, external storage, external identity); adding a major library/framework or replacing approved baseline technology; introducing a project-wide convention or abstraction (e.g. a project-wide Result model); changing the authentication/authorization architecture; a breaking public API change.

When SPECIFICATION.md or CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md changes, keep the two consistent; CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md changes run custom-settings to synchronize every affected surface; approved behavior changes follow development-workflow.
modality: SHOULD (PostToolUse feedback after editing product inputs; Stop reminder once per change state)
exceptions: Stop reminder only inside a Git work tree and repeated only when the changed files or their content differ.

normative_action: When Domain or persistence model files (Domain .cs, Infrastructure Persistence/Configurations, *DbContext.cs) changed without a seeder change, confirm seeded entities are unaffected or update the seeder, or state why the reminder does not apply.
modality: SHOULD (Stop hook: Claude continues once per change state)
trigger_scope: Stop in a Git work tree
exceptions: Repeated only when the changed files or their relevant content change; never loops (stop_hook_active).

normative_action: When migration files changed, review each generated migration before committing.
modality: SHOULD (Stop hook reminder once per change state)
trigger_scope: Stop in a Git work tree

normative_action: When backend or frontend production code changed without any backend or frontend test change, confirm equivalent coverage exists or add tests (development-workflow, verify step 4) before finishing.
modality: SHOULD (Stop hook reminder once per change state)
trigger_scope: Stop in a Git work tree
exceptions: Same repetition limits as RULE-L0-0009; outside Git the reminder is unavailable (visible, non-blocking).

normative_action: Project-reference graph changes: every 'dotnet add/remove ... reference' and 'dotnet reference add/remove' command is blocked before it runs; references mapped by layout.md follow project-structure, any other reference-graph change needs a Decision Request (architecture-decision) and an approved change is applied in the project file; every added or removed ProjectReference and every added, moved or removed project file is reported for confirmation against the layout or an approved decision and must be reported.
modality: REQUIRES_APPROVAL (Reserved; PreToolUse blocks every reference command; post-bash and post-edit report every reference change)
trigger_scope: .NET project references and project files in the active worktree
exceptions: Layout-mapped references are not Reserved but must be written into the project file because the CLI path is always blocked.
why_extra_or_uncertain: ARC-020 requires approval for new layers/projects and ARC-001 fixes direction; no oracle policy makes individual reference edges between existing projects Reserved or forbids the CLI route for approved or layout references.

normative_action: Every dependency change reports the results of its version, deprecation, vulnerability and license checks (hook feedback: 'report them'; add-dependency report).
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-003/DEP-004 require the checks; WF-009 covers verification reporting only; no oracle policy requires reporting dependency due-diligence results.

normative_action: Level model of the instruction system: every instruction artifact carries a header (Level, Owns, Scope, Loads, Depends on); rules live in level directories with paths front matter; conformance dependencies ('Depends on') point only to the same or a more stable level without cycles; Levels 0 and 1 name no concrete technology beyond .NET, C#, TypeScript (Git for repository safety); every artifact is listed in the instruction map; after editing CLAUDE.md or .claude/**/*.md|json|mjs the structure checker runs and every reported error must be fixed.
modality: MUST (checker-enforced; PostToolUse feedback after instruction edits)
exceptions: Routing pointers ('run verify', 'see layout.md') are not conformance dependencies.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system organization rule of the L0 template; the oracle defines no level hierarchy, header format or technology-neutrality requirement for instruction files.

normative_action: When resilience is required the Microsoft resilience packages are the default; direct Polly is an explicit exception that needs a recorded decision or a reported reason.
modality: DEFAULT (manifest check: flagged unless an accepted decision names it)
exceptions: Package id listed in an '## Accepted' section of decisions.md or overview.md.

normative_action: MediatR and Kommand packages are flagged because mediator-based organization is not adopted (Reserved).
exceptions: Accepted decision recorded in the decision summaries.

normative_action: AutoMapper (another mapping framework) requires approval; it is flagged unless an accepted decision names it.
@ngrx/store, axios, lodash, bootstrap and tailwindcss are not added by default; package.json entries are flagged unless a recorded decision or concrete need exists.
modality: MUST NOT (by default; manifest check finding)
exceptions: Accepted decision or reported concrete need.

normative_action: Build and test tooling (Angular CLI/build/devkit/compiler-cli, TypeScript, Vitest, Playwright test, ESLint, Prettier, Karma, Jasmine, @types) belongs in devDependencies, not in runtime dependencies.

Production project references point inward: Domain references no application project; Application references Domain; Infrastructure references Application and Domain; Api references Application, Infrastructure and Domain; no production project references a test project.
trigger_scope: backend .csproj files (layer from the project-name suffix)
exceptions: Test projects (names ending in Test/Tests) are not checked; Api -> Domain is allowed by the check.

normative_action: Package versions are never empty, floating (*, latest, x) or prerelease (alpha, beta, preview, rc, dev, nightly, pre) unless explicitly requested.
NuGet Central Package Management: PackageReference entries carry no Version; VersionOverride needs a reported concrete reason; ManagePackageVersionsCentrally stays true in Directory.Packages.props.

Packages Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly and Polly.Extensions.Http (deprecated resilience integrations) and Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch (deprecated sink) must not be added; they are reported on every manifest validation.
modality: MUST NOT (manifest check finding; no approval path)
exceptions: none stated (accepted decisions do not exempt deny-listed packages)
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-004 requires checking deprecation and DEP-020 treats direct Polly integration as an explicit exception; no oracle policy forbids specific packages outright regardless of approval.

normative_action: Do not adopt a deprecated or legacy ASP.NET automatic-validation integration package (FluentValidation.AspNetCore) unless a concrete project requirement justifies it; deviation needs a recorded decision or reported reason.
modality: DEFAULT (manifest check: flagged unless an accepted decision names it)
exceptions: Concrete project requirement recorded as an accepted decision.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-010 fixes FluentValidation as the library and DEP-004 requires deprecation checks; no oracle policy restricts its ASP.NET integration package.

normative_action: SPECIFICATION.md, CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, feature specifications and task prompts are product inputs, not instruction layers: they define behavior and approved values and may request an engineering decision change, but never silently override engineering policy.

Inspect relevant existing code before non-trivial changes and apply the applicable rules; workflows explicitly read the rule files they depend on because path rules may not have fired (for example in a new repository).

Add a dependency only for a concrete current requirement of the change at hand; never install packages for hypothetical future use; 'approved' or 'conditional' in the project decisions does not mean 'install by default'.
Keep each dependency in the narrowest project or workspace that actually requires it.

Keep changes focused on the requested scope and preserve existing behavior unless the task or approved specification requires a change (e.g. no unrelated dependency cleanup during a narrowly scoped task).
exceptions: Task or approved specification requires change.

normative_action: Never log passwords, access or refresh tokens, private keys, authentication secrets or full payment credentials; avoid personal data without a concrete permitted operational need; a lower log level does not make sensitive data safe.
Do not serialize arbitrary request bodies, domain objects or sensitive payloads into logs by default; log the minimum operationally useful, non-sensitive context.
Log an unexpected exception once, at the boundary that handles it, not again in every layer it passes through.
Prefer clear, correct code first; no specialized optimizations without a concrete reason; prefer measurement or profiling evidence for non-trivial optimization.
Introduce precompiled queries, specialized async return types, pooling, custom serialization, aggressive caching or raw SQL for performance only for a measured or clearly demonstrated need.
Keep database access efficient: filter and project in the database when practical, avoid unnecessary round trips, over-fetching and N+1 patterns, paginate potentially large result sets.
Caching is not a default architecture requirement; introduce it only for a clear measured or reasoned need and choose the implementation by deployment, consistency and staleness requirements.
Cache keys uniquely represent the cached value and include every relevant user, tenant and context dimension; avoid global keys for user- or tenant-specific data.
Invalidate or update cache entries only consistently with successful underlying mutations; the cache must not become a second source of truth.
Every cache entry has a lifetime or another explicit invalidation strategy.
External I/O calls have a bounded execution time appropriate to the operation; avoid overlapping timeout mechanisms whose combined behavior is unclear.
Retry only when repeating the operation is safe; never automatically retry state-changing operations without idempotency or another concrete duplicate-safety mechanism.
Respect Retry-After or equivalent rate-limit guidance where appropriate; do not retry indefinitely or aggressively.
Use a fallback only when its result is semantically acceptable; never hide correctness failures behind convenient default values.
Caller cancellation is not a transient dependency failure: do not classify it as one or convert it into repeated outbound attempts.
Normal client-request cancellation is not a server failure: do not map it to a generic 500 or log it as an unhandled application failure.
Health checks stay cheap and deterministic; they do not become business workflows or perform expensive or mutating database work.

Liveness and readiness keep distinct dependency semantics: liveness avoids external dependencies that could cause restart loops; readiness may depend on capabilities required to serve traffic and reflects startup and dependency availability.

Never hardcode or commit real secrets, credentials, private keys, access/refresh tokens or production connection strings, including in example configuration files, Dockerfiles, committed Compose files and build arguments.

Use an appropriate local secret mechanism in development and environment-specific secret injection or a managed secret store in deployed environments; do not assume a cloud provider the project has not chosen.

Treat data crossing the trusted boundary (HTTP requests, uploaded files, external responses, message payloads, user identifiers and filters) as untrusted and validate it at the owning layer when assumptions matter.
Do not trust client-provided file metadata such as MIME type as authoritative when upload handling or a security decision depends on actual content.
Use parameterized database access; never build SQL by concatenating untrusted input.
Enforce authorization on the server; frontend route guards, hidden buttons and client checks are user experience, not a security boundary.
Anonymous access is deliberate and visible; avoid redundant authorization markers when a secure global or fallback policy already expresses the intent.

Do not implement custom token or password security, password hashing or reset-token cryptography when the platform's established authentication and identity facilities (ASP.NET Core authentication handlers, ASP.NET Core Identity) cover the requirement.
For Bearer/OIDC validate what the actual issuer/provider requires (issuer, audience where applicable, signature/signing authority, lifetime); never disable validation to make a token work.
Do not expose authentication-failure detail that unnecessarily reveals secrets or account state; avoid account-enumeration leaks where relevant.
When browser cookies carry authentication credentials automatically, include CSRF protection in the design; a single-page frontend does not remove the risk.
Do not claim one browser token-storage mechanism is universally secure; choose storage by threat model and never log tokens.
Production traffic carrying credentials or sensitive data uses TLS; respect the hosting topology and never disable certificate validation to make an integration work.
Do not implement custom cryptography when a well-reviewed platform mechanism is appropriate; do not treat ASP.NET Core Data Protection as universal database encryption.
Configure CORS to the narrowest policy satisfying actual browser-client requirements; never combine credentialed cross-origin requests with unrestricted origins.
Security-sensitive authorization, permission or required-control checks fail safely; do not silently convert lookup or configuration failures into success.
When a required security control cannot be configured correctly, prefer a visible startup or configuration failure over an insecure fallback.
Do not expose stack traces, SQL details, connection strings, internal paths, secret values or sensitive exception details in public API errors.
Do not expose secrets, credentials, connection details, stack traces or unnecessary internal diagnostics through publicly reachable health responses.

Choose the narrowest test level that meaningfully verifies the behavior; integration tests when framework wiring, HTTP, persistence, serialization, authentication or component interaction is the subject; no fixed ratio.

Tests verify observable behavior and survive internal refactoring; no unnecessary dependence on private methods, exact internal call sequences, specific implementation classes or incidental details; no reproduced algorithms; interaction verification only when the interaction is the specified behavior.

When provider behavior matters, test against the actual database provider; never claim provider fidelity from a test running on a different provider (EF Core InMemory is not relational and never verifies relational or SQL Server behavior).

Tests are deterministic, independent of execution order and isolated from Production and Development data, uncontrolled external systems and shared mutable state; the Testing environment uses isolated resources.
Tests start from a known state and own their setup; they never depend on development seeding or on other tests having run.
For small finite input/state spaces prefer explicit declarative cases over loops, branching, LINQ or generated case machinery; state expected results instead of computing them.
Use descriptive test names communicating scenario/condition and expected behavior (e.g. MethodOrScenario_Condition_ExpectedBehavior); follow an established project convention.
Do not generate low-value tests merely to increase a coverage percentage; coverage is diagnostic, not a target.
Domain stays independent of persistence frameworks, web/transport frameworks, HTTP, persistence and external-service implementation concerns (entity mappings live in Infrastructure).

Simple domain entities by default; use-case and workflow rules live in Application Services; validation rules, immutable fields, status transitions or allowed/forbidden edits do not by themselves justify a Rich Domain Model.

Move behavior into Domain only when non-trivial invariants materially benefit from domain-level encapsulation independently of a use case; otherwise a Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical pattern requires approval unless the approved specification already requires it.

Do not add factory methods, private setters, transition methods, Aggregate Roots, Domain Events, Specifications, Domain Services, systematic Value Objects or similar DDD constructs merely to make a simple model look domain-driven.

Application Services are the default orchestration mechanism for use cases (coordinating Domain objects, repositories, external-service abstractions and the Unit of Work); a growing service signals responsibility review, not automatic adoption of another pattern.

Persistence and external-service abstractions (repository interfaces) are inward-facing contracts defined in Application when use cases require them and implemented in Infrastructure; infrastructure details stay out of Application.

Application must not depend on persistence-framework types or APIs (DbContext, DbSet<T>, EF APIs and expressions, EF attributes, SQL Server provider types) or web-framework transport types (IActionResult, ActionResult<T>, ProblemDetails, HttpContext, ClaimsPrincipal, IHttpContextAccessor, StatusCodes).
Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into the Application-facing abstraction; HttpResponseMessage and other remote-transport concerns do not leak into Application.
Keep cache technology out of Domain and do not leak infrastructure cache APIs into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.
Program.cs in Api is the composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations.
Keep registration close to the owning layer: Application registers Application services (incl. its validators), Infrastructure registers persistence and adapters, Api remains the composition root.
Use constructor injection for required dependencies; avoid service-locator and property-injection patterns.
Respect dependency lifetimes: never capture a shorter-lived dependency inside a longer-lived service.
Physical structure follows actual responsibilities: no speculative projects, infrastructure, empty directory trees or generic Common/Helpers/Utils buckets solely to look architectural.
Backend test projects receive no broader production-project references than their test scope requires; they follow the inward dependency discipline.
HTTP entry points are thin: bind and validate HTTP input, invoke Application services and translate Application outcomes into HTTP responses.
Entry points contain no business logic, do not access the persistence context or concrete repositories, and do not construct infrastructure services manually.
HTTP status codes and transport response semantics belong to Api; Application and Domain must not return web-framework result types or HTTP status codes.
Do not duplicate equivalent DTOs across Api and Application merely to create layer-shaped types; introduce transport-specific contracts when separation gives a concrete boundary benefit.
HTTP failures use a structured problem-details error contract (ProblemDetails; ValidationProblemDetails for request validation) whose machine-readable parts stay stable and safe.
Choose 200/201/202/204 by actual HTTP semantics; never 200 for every outcome, 201 merely for an internal insert, or 202 for completed work.
A successful collection query with zero matches returns 200 with an empty collection, not 404.
401 for missing or failed authentication, 403 for an authenticated principal not permitted; hiding a resource with 404 requires a deliberate, consistent security policy.
409 for a valid request conflicting with current state; 412 when an explicit HTTP precondition such as If-Match fails.
Do not introduce API versioning merely because an API exists; add it when published compatibility or coexisting client generations create a concrete need.
Once external clients rely on an API version, avoid silent breaking changes; a breaking change requires a new version or another explicitly approved compatibility strategy.
When explicit versioning is required, use one strategy consistently; URL-segment versioning unless requirements justify another.
Do not create separate Domain or persistence models merely because the external API has several versions; isolate version-specific transport contracts at the Api boundary when practical.

Deprecating or removing a published API version follows architecture-decision: mark the deprecation in versioning metadata, document the replacement, communicate a realistic migration/removal timeline and keep the old version working for the promised support period.
API documentation metadata describes the API that actually runs (routes, important response statuses, schemas, authentication behavior); do not document speculative responses.
Organize frontend application code primarily by feature; avoid application-wide technical buckets and empty architecture folders; keep feature-specific code within its feature and core/shared small.
Route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; do not lazy-load every tiny component.
Pages and components stay focused on presentation and UI orchestration; do not move trivial presentation logic into services merely to shrink components.

Keep backend communication in explicit feature data-access services or another explicit HTTP boundary; do not scatter HTTP calls through presentation components; never import backend Domain types; use frontend API models matching the published HTTP contract.
Prefer simple local, component or service state before introducing a state-management library.
Frontend code follows the documented API error contract; centralize reusable problem-details parsing when practical; never infer business behavior from human-readable exception messages.
Use reactive forms for non-trivial forms when useful; frontend validation improves UX but never replaces backend validation or data-integrity and security enforcement.

Represent common expected outcomes explicitly when useful (null, bool, a typed outcome, or a deliberately adopted Result model) with the simplest contract; do not force a generic Result<T> pattern; no HTTP-named outcome categories in Application — describe Application semantics and map them to HTTP in Api.
Do not establish custom business exceptions as the default architecture, and do not throw and catch exceptions merely to jump between normal expected branches.

Unexpected failures propagate to centralized boundary handling (IExceptionHandler with AddProblemDetails/UseExceptionHandler); avoid repetitive catch/log/rethrow blocks; catch only to recover, translate, perform a defined fallback, add context or clean up; do not swallow failures.

Validate each concern at the owning layer: Api validates transport and request-contract concerns, Application use-case and straightforward workflow rules, Domain genuine invariants, Infrastructure external-system assumptions; no mechanical duplication of a rule across layers and no Domain invariants moved into request validators.

Adopted architecture: backend Clean Architecture with four layers and inward dependencies (Domain business concepts; Application use-case orchestration and inward abstractions; Infrastructure persistence and external-service implementations; Api entry points and composition root); the frontend is a separate client workspace that communicates with the backend only through the published HTTP API and is organized by feature.
CQRS handlers, mediator-based organization (with any mediator library) and Vertical Slice Architecture are not adopted; introducing them requires approval.

Reviews prioritize real defects (correctness, security, data integrity, architecture, concurrency/integration, meaningful tests, maintainability, credible performance) over style and must not require or enforce patterns the architecture has not adopted.

The persistence framework is an Infrastructure implementation detail: use it normally inside Infrastructure (concrete repositories may use the full EF Core API) but do not leak its concepts into Application; do not cripple repository implementations to preserve a generic abstraction.

Prefer specific repository interfaces representing cohesive Application persistence needs over table-mirroring generic CRUD contracts; Aggregate Roots of an explicitly approved DDD design are natural repository boundaries.

Repository interfaces must not expose IQueryable<T>, persistence-framework context, set or query-expression types, or provider-specific types; query construction stays in Infrastructure and contracts return materialized results.

Application must not depend on IGenericRepository<T> or another generic CRUD contract; a generic repository or base class (e.g. an Infrastructure-only Repository<TEntity>) may exist only in Infrastructure to remove real duplication; use-case-specific queries belong in concrete repositories.

IUnitOfWork is the normal commit boundary of an Application use case: repositories stage changes and Application Services decide when to commit; its Infrastructure implementation delegates to the shared scoped DbContext.

Repositories participating in one use case share the same scoped Unit of Work and persistence context; repositories are injected explicitly; IUnitOfWork must not become a repository container or service locator.
Do not introduce explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case requires control beyond the normal single save/commit.
Use modern standalone Angular APIs for new code; do not introduce NgModules for ordinary new feature work unless an integration or legacy dependency requires them.
Use Signals for naturally synchronous local UI state and RxJS when asynchronous streams, HTTP composition, cancellation or event pipelines are clearer; avoid mechanical conversions.
Avoid manual nested RxJS subscriptions; prefer composition operators when they express the behavior clearly.
When manually subscribing from Angular framework-managed code, tie the subscription lifetime to the component or service lifecycle with the project's current Angular facilities.
Prefer functional HTTP interceptors for new code and keep interceptor responsibilities cross-cutting; never put feature business logic in an interceptor.

Use frontend scripts and runners that actually exist (inspect package.json instead of assuming a command); never invent npm scripts; in CI use npm ci when a maintained lockfile supports it and do not reflexively replace lockfile-based installs.
Api entry points are ASP.NET Core Controllers; do not create Minimal API endpoint groups unless explicitly requested.
Enable Swagger UI in Development and expose it elsewhere only when deployment requirements explicitly justify it.
Docker is optional infrastructure: do not introduce it merely because the application can be containerized; add container artifacts only when the project or deployment needs them.

Production containers use an appropriate runtime image (the ASP.NET runtime image) rather than the SDK image for convenience, run as the image's non-root user where supported, do not switch to root to bypass permission problems, keep build tooling out of runtime images and keep environment configuration external.
Follow the repository's existing conventions and .editorconfig (including its established invocation patterns); use modern C# when it improves clarity, but do not mechanically modernize working code.
Do not perform style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked; avoid mixing large formatting or modernization changes with functional work.

For new code prefer file-scoped namespaces when consistent, one primary top-level type per file with a matching name, and the Async suffix for Task/ValueTask-returning methods unless an existing or framework contract makes that inappropriate.
Use async APIs for asynchronous I/O and never block them with .Result, .Wait() or similar sync-over-async patterns.
Propagate CancellationToken through asynchronous operations when cancellation is meaningful; no cancellation parameters on purely synchronous code without a use case.
Use TimeProvider for application logic that depends on the current clock and needs deterministic testing; do not mechanically replace explicit or stored timestamps.
Never create and dispose a new HttpClient per request; use IHttpClientFactory or another appropriate long-lived strategy.

Prefer strongly typed options for structured configuration and validate settings at startup when missing or invalid values prevent correct or secure operation; avoid scattered string-based IConfiguration lookups.
NUnit is the default .NET test framework; no second test framework without a concrete reason; in an established project deliberately using another framework follow its convention.

Use WebApplicationFactory<Program>-based integration tests when routing, binding, middleware, authentication/authorization, DI, repositories, EF Core or database persistence is what the test must prove.
EF Core with the SQL Server provider is the persistence framework of the approved stack; provider-specific concerns stay out of Application and Domain.
FluentValidation is the standard explicit request/use-case validation library; application logging uses ILogger<T> with Serilog as provider.

Placement and ownership of instruction content: rule = normative constraint, workflow skill = procedure, knowledge skill = technique (never the sole owner of a rule), product files = inputs, hooks/scripts/config = deterministic enforcement; each rule has exactly one owner and other files point to it; planning-time rules go to CLAUDE.md or a decision summary, file-scoped rules to a path rule covering at least their scope; maintenance runs template-maintenance.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system placement and ownership rules; the oracle does not regulate where instruction content lives or how it is owned.

normative_action: Hook registration form: hooks are registered in exec form (command node, args with the ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} placeholder, no shell); PreToolUse Bash|PowerShell runs pre-bash with onFailure block; PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure Bash|PowerShell run post-bash; PostToolUse Edit|MultiEdit|Write runs post-edit; Stop runs stop; only the PreToolUse hook fails closed.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Hook-configuration design of the template; no oracle policy regulates hook registration or failure semantics.

normative_action: Accepted decisions are recorded in the decision summary of their level (architecture decisions in overview.md, project/stack decisions in decisions.md) with date, decision, scope, consequences and the owning rule updated; approved exceptions for review-listed packages take effect only through these 'Accepted' sections.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 requires approval for Reserved decisions but no recording format; GOV-007 covers product behavior sources. No oracle policy requires level-stratified decision summaries or makes package exceptions depend on them.

normative_action: Application-level validators live in Application and are registered with FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions from Application's own registration.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-010 fixes FluentValidation and API-010 the validation boundaries; no oracle policy prescribes the registration package.

normative_action: Use ILogger<T> with structured message templates and stable property names; avoid string interpolation that turns structured values into opaque text.

When Serilog is configured use the DI-integrated builder.Services.AddSerilog(...) approach (not UseSerilog()), keep levels, sinks and overrides in environment-aware configuration, and keep application code on ILogger<T> rather than Serilog APIs.
For an empty Development database maintain a small deterministic, representative seed dataset covering the meaningful states and relationships.
Development seeding is an Infrastructure/bootstrap concern: it may use AppDbContext directly and need not go through Application repositories or IUnitOfWork.

Keep substantial seed construction in a dedicated internal DbSeeder (e.g. Infrastructure/Persistence/Seeding/DbSeeder.cs) invoked through a narrow Infrastructure initialization extension, not in Program.cs, AppDbContext configuration, entity configurations or migrations.
Automatic development seeding runs only in the Development environment; never seed Production automatically; tests own their setup and never use the seeder.
The seeder must not call Database.Migrate() or EnsureCreated() or otherwise create or upgrade schema; migrations are applied separately before seeding.

If representative data already exists, leave it unchanged; never use the seeder for automatic synchronization, repair, upgrade, overwrite or recreation of an existing Development database; developers recreate the local database explicitly.
Seed entities preserve current Domain invariants and valid relationships; prefer readable deterministic examples over exhaustive or random combinations.

For the SQL Server baseline appsettings.Development.json provides a usable local Development connection string when it contains no secret credentials (e.g. LocalDB with Trusted_Connection); credential-bearing local values come from user-secrets or another approved local secret mechanism.
When an approved technology covers a need, use it rather than silently selecting an alternative; replacing one is Reserved.
Backend platform: .NET 10 LTS (latest stable servicing release), C# 14, ASP.NET Core, ASP.NET Core Controllers; moving to a preview/RC .NET or C# release requires approval.

Swashbuckle Swagger UI is the default Development interactive documentation and manual-testing surface; exposure beyond Development follows the ASP.NET Core binding (only when deployment requirements justify it).

Backend tests: NUnit; backend test projects live under backend/ beside the production projects; Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing / WebApplicationFactory<Program> is the integration-test baseline; Testcontainers is conditional (only when isolated real-provider tests justify it).
Frontend: current stable Angular with CLI-selected compatible TypeScript and RxJS; standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, zoneless mode when supported, SCSS, Angular Material and CDK, Vitest.

Conditional technologies are added only when their trigger holds: Mapster (+ Mapster.DependencyInjection) when mapping volume is repetitive or non-trivial (manual mapping is fine for simple cases); Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience / Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience when a real integration needs resilience.
Playwright is the approved default when frontend E2E coverage is required, but not part of the minimal scaffold.

Do not add NgRx, Axios, Lodash, Bootstrap, Tailwind or additional form, component or state-management libraries by default; use built-in Angular capabilities first and add an extra library only for a concrete need.
Use the .slnx solution format by default; legacy .sln only when an external tool or project requirement requires it.
Repository-level Directory.Build.props holds genuinely shared .NET build settings and Directory.Packages.props the CPM versions; project-specific settings stay in their owning projects.

Physical layout: backend production and test projects under backend/<Name>.<Layer>/, the Angular workspace under frontend/<Name>.Web/ (unit and component tests inside the workspace, E2E under frontend/<Name>.Web/e2e/, never under backend/), maintained documentation under docs/; keep them separated and create no top-level tests/ directory.
Layer-to-project mapping: Domain = backend/<Name>.Domain/, Application = backend/<Name>.Application/, Infrastructure = backend/<Name>.Infrastructure/, Api = backend/<Name>.Api/ (contains Program.cs).

Use npm for the Angular workspace unless the project deliberately adopts another package manager; keep package-lock.json consistent with every change; install with the correct category (build/test tooling in devDependencies).

Before installation check that the exact selected version is not deprecated, review known vulnerability information and verify its license from official registry metadata (and upstream when necessary); permissive licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD) may normally be accepted; a free download does not make a package acceptable.

Do not automatically install a paid/commercial dependency or one with a materially restrictive or unclassifiable license; explain the concern and present options (say so when no free alternative exists) without silently substituting; no legal conclusions beyond the published license.

When Controller API versioning is explicitly adopted use the Controller integration of Asp.Versioning (Asp.Versioning.Mvc, plus Asp.Versioning.Mvc.ApiExplorer); do not add it before the project actually adopts versioning.

Prefer simple, maintainable solutions; keep architectural complexity proportional to current requirements and avoid speculative abstractions (e.g. no custom wrapper around every UI-library component without a concrete reason).

Treat generated code as generated: keep it separate from handwritten code, regenerate it when its source contract changes and do not patch generated files unless the generation workflow requires it; fix wrong generated output at its source.
exceptions: Generation workflow treats output as maintained source.

normative_action: Classify every consequential choice: Decided (settled by the instruction system, product inputs or a recorded decision, including choices already required by the specification or the established project structure; follow it, do not reopen without approval), Delegated (local, reversible, no change to a boundary, dependency, accepted convention, public contract or observable behavior; decide and proceed), Reserved (explicit approval before implementation); an explicit user instruction counts as approval.

For a Reserved decision present a Decision Request (Context, Options, Recommendation, Blocked, Proceeding with), then run architecture-decision; do not implement the Reserved option before approval and continue only with the 'Proceeding with' work.
In an autonomous or headless run take only a policy-compliant non-Reserved path, never make a Reserved decision silently, and list every unresolved Decision Request explicitly in the final report.
When an accepted decision changes product behavior, synchronize the durable product inputs (SPECIFICATION.md, CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md) in the same change.
Commit package.json and package-lock.json and keep the lockfile consistent with every change.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Read as a version-control content convention the clause is entailed by DEP-007; read as an instruction to perform commits it conflicts with GOV-015 (commits only on explicit request). The text does not settle the reading.

normative_action: Removing a dependency removes the project reference and, when no project uses it any more, its central version in Directory.Packages.props, then rebuilds and runs the affected tests.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-001..DEP-006 govern additions and central version placement; no oracle policy prescribes a removal procedure or the cleanup of unused central versions.

normative_action: Adopting API versioning is Reserved and needs explicit approval, even when a concrete compatibility need exists.
why_extra_or_uncertain: API-013 allows introducing versioning when a real compatibility need exists and does not require approval; the oracle's consequential-change list does not name versioning adoption.

normative_action: Decision reporting: Delegated decisions taken are mentioned in the report, and a rejected Decision Request is not recorded as a decision but mentioned in the report.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 requires classification and reporting of unresolved Decision Requests in headless runs; no oracle policy requires reporting Delegated decisions or rejected requests.

normative_action: Build-fix starts from reproduction and diagnosis: reproduce with the narrowest command, read the complete output, group errors by root cause and fix the highest-leverage cause first; decide for failing tests whether production code, setup, expectation, environment or an intentional contract change is at fault; determine the authoritative contract instead of patching both sides of a cross-stack break; update obsolete APIs from verified documentation, never invented.

Repair in small bounded iterations: rerun the narrowest failing verification after each meaningful fix, expand only after the focused failure is resolved, do not run unrelated build systems, use several focused attempts rather than an unlimited loop and stop when progress stalls instead of making speculative edits.

Never weaken, delete, skip or suppress relevant tests or compiler, TypeScript, lint or analyzer failures to make verification pass (no strong-to-weak assertion swaps, no any-casts or disabled strict mode to silence errors); update a test only for an intentionally requested contract change.

A green build obtained by violating the architecture (outward or invalid project references, persistence types in Application, business logic in Controllers, Angular-only authorization, HTTP calls scattered into components) is not a successful repair; preserve architecture and project conventions while fixing.

When verification fails make the smallest appropriate fix and rerun until green or genuine user input is required; never claim a problem fixed while a known relevant failure remains, never leave the repository knowingly worse, and when the required toolchain is unavailable report the limitation instead of editing source or changing declared SDK/Node/framework versions.
exceptions: Unrelated pre-existing failures are left alone unless they block verification or the user asks.

normative_action: Report verification state with PASS / NOT RUN / NOT APPLICABLE per area; never imply that an unchecked area passed.

Do not introduce frameworks, libraries, infrastructure or architectural patterns without a concrete current need (e.g. pipeline stages or CI services for parts that do not exist, distributed caches merely because caching exists).

CI definitions stay in source control, reproduce the repository's supported build and test commands for the parts that actually exist and never hide build or test failures (no continue-on-error on build/test steps, no suppressed exit codes, no skipped failing tests); formatting/analyzer gates only when adopted; restore from a clean environment without developer-machine state.

Do not apply production database migrations automatically from normal application startup (in containers or anywhere else); production migration is an explicit, visible deployment step at a controlled point with approved credentials; deployment never runs Development seeding in Production.

Never invent review findings to populate categories or failures without a plausible execution path; when there are no meaningful findings, say so and state the important areas that could not be verified.
When SPECIFICATION.md is non-empty it is authoritative for project-specific functional requirements and observable product behavior; an empty template file is intentional.

Do not silently weaken, contradict or materially extend approved behavior; do not invent user-visible behavior, limits, defaults, restrictions or workflows (new limits, reserved values, required fields, extra validation), also not merely because the specification does not forbid them.

String semantics are product behavior when observable (case sensitivity, collation, culture vs ordinal, normalization, trimming, uniqueness, lookup); when product sources do not define them and the choice affects equality, uniqueness, lookup or accepted input, ask for approval instead of choosing silently, including through database configuration or framework defaults.

Run the full security-scan only when the user requested a security audit, the change is materially security-sensitive, or a concrete finding justifies broader investigation; run architecture, formatting/analyzer, dependency and security checks according to the change's risk.
For a meaningful bug with plausible recurrence add a regression test (failing before, passing after the fix) unless equivalent coverage exists; do not request duplicate tests.
Behavior established with a temporary or manual probe is preserved in maintained automated coverage (verify step 4) unless equivalent coverage exists.

Compiler diagnostics, analyzers, IDE tooling, scanners and repository search are evidence, not authority; no MCP server or specific analyzer is required; read the code before turning a tool warning into a finding.

When a CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md value is added, changed or removed, search for and update every affected implementation, validation, configuration, test, documentation and mirrored frontend/backend surface (backend validation authoritative, frontend kept in sync for UX), search for stale references and run the normal verification; changing one literal alone does not establish synchronization.

SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict each other; confirm consistency before changing a value and re-check afterwards; if they conflict, stop and resolve which source must be corrected before continuing.

CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md holds approved project-level tunable limits and defaults (maximum lengths, page-size defaults and maximums, retention periods, numeric thresholds) under stable descriptive names with value and purpose; SPECIFICATION.md owns behavioral intent.

When a settings change affects schema constraints, indexes, column lengths or other persistence metadata: update the EF Core mapping, create the appropriate new migration per the project's migration workflow (regenerate or edit only an uncommitted migration when that matches the workflow; do not casually alter existing migrations), verify Development seeding remains valid, and add or update provider-sensitive tests when needed.
The build-fix report states the initial failure, root cause, changes made, backend build / frontend build / tests status (PASS, NOT RUN, NOT APPLICABLE) and remaining issues.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 requires reporting actual verification states only; no oracle policy prescribes failure/root-cause/changes sections.

normative_action: Code-review findings are reported ordered by severity with severity, file/location, problem, why it matters and smallest reasonable fix, on the scale Critical (data loss, security vulnerability, reliably broken core behavior; blocks merge), High, Medium, Low.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-011/WF-012 set priorities and forbid manufactured findings; the oracle prescribes no output format or severity scale.

normative_action: Do not cache EF tracked entities across Unit of Work boundaries (named caching anti-pattern).
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-021 governs invalidation consistency and ARC-019 confines EF Core to Infrastructure; caching tracked entities is an EF technique pitfall (EXC-011 class) that the template turns into a named prohibition.

normative_action: For substantial feature work or a newly implemented application run code-review (or the code-reviewer agent) before the final verification and address real findings.
Before declaring implementation complete run verify; a change is not complete while verification fails or is unreported.

A performance-motivated change identifies the actual bottleneck or cost, preserves observable behavior, uses the simplest effective optimization, keeps or adds tests for the affected behavior, and benchmarks or profiles non-obvious or complex optimizations.
For a new application or substantial feature read SPECIFICATION.md (and any feature specification) before planning or implementing; read CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md when tunable values are involved.

Before implementing a questionable request name the concrete concern (duplication, poor cohesion, trigger or loading problems, context cost, conflict with architecture or policy, unnecessary complexity) and propose an alternative; this never authorizes silently rewriting or ignoring the user's requirement — the user decides.

Whenever a Domain or persistence change affects seeded entities (new required or renamed properties, changed relationships or enum/status values, new meaningful states, changed invariants), update the maintained development seeder in the same change so that recreating the Development database at this revision yields valid, representative data.

Treat migrations as source code: review each generated migration before committing it, paying particular attention to destructive schema changes, unexpected column recreation, data migrations, indexes, foreign keys and delete behavior.
Schema changes are created as new EF Core migrations from the Infrastructure project with the Api project as startup project.
why_extra_or_uncertain: The oracle requires a migration only for schema-affecting CUSTOM_SETTINGS changes (PST-009) and review of generated migrations (PST-010); it has no general rule that every schema change is made through a new migration with fixed projects.

normative_action: The development-workflow report summarizes what changed, the verify result block, unresolved Decision Requests and remaining known issues.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 covers the verification state and GOV-017 the listing of unresolved Decision Requests in headless runs; a fixed summary of changes and remaining known issues for every implementation is an additional reporting duty.

normative_action: Do not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete or rename branches or perform other repository-changing Git operations unless explicitly requested; never force-push a shared branch unless the user explicitly requests history rewriting.
Parallel implementation streams use separate branches and worktrees (one branch is not checked out in several normal worktrees); keep unrelated changes out of the current branch.

Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier; never remove a worktree containing uncommitted user work; do not automatically stash, reset or discard local work for a merge or rebase.

Before any repository-changing operation inspect the relevant state (status, diffs, what a high-risk operation would lose or rewrite) and use the minimum operation required; do not silently clean up unrelated working-tree changes.

Before committing inspect the staged diff and include only the requested logical change; do not stage unrelated modified files; one logical change per commit with its tests, no artificial tiny commits or combined unrelated fixes; before pushing confirm branch and state, ensure relevant verification completed and avoid pushing unrelated local commits.

git reset --hard, git clean, git push --force / --force-with-lease, branch deletion and rebasing shared history are performed only when explicitly requested or clearly required by an approved workflow, after inspecting what will be lost or rewritten.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-015 permits repository-changing Git operations only on explicit request; 'clearly required by an approved workflow' names no workflow and may authorize high-risk operations without an explicit request, or may only refer to an explicitly approved procedure.

normative_action: Treat main, master and other protected/shared branches as non-rewritable.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-015 allows repository-changing operations, including history rewriting, on explicit request; this rule forbids rewriting these branches without an approval path.

normative_action: A pull request has a focused purpose and its description explains what changed, why, how it was verified, and compatibility/migration notes.
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy prescribes PR description contents; WF-009 only requires truthful verification reporting.

normative_action: Do not make fire-and-forget EF Core async calls (named anti-pattern).
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-002 concerns blocking on async I/O and ARC-017 the shared scoped context; no oracle policy names unawaited (fire-and-forget) EF calls, which is EF technique turned into a prohibition.

normative_action: Do not wrap normal EF Core operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline; prefer the provider's EF Core execution strategy (e.g. EnableRetryOnFailure for SQL Server) and follow provider guidance for transaction/retry interaction.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-016 governs when retries are safe and the oracle treats database-retry examples as conditional technique (EXC-007); no oracle policy forbids an application-level retry pipeline around EF Core operations.

normative_action: Never mutate a shared HttpClient's DefaultRequestHeaders concurrently; apply per-request values such as dynamic tokens per request or through a handler.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-005 governs client lifetime only; thread-safe header handling is client technique not stated by any oracle policy.

normative_action: Scaffolding creates global.json pinning the intended SDK line: the current stable SDK of the target release (no preview/RC line unless approved) with a rollForward policy that allows normal patch/feature-band servicing.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-008 fixes the platform and DEP-023 repository-level build configuration; no oracle policy requires a global.json SDK pin or a particular roll-forward policy.

normative_action: Security review is evidence-based: report concrete risks in the context of actual exposure, distinguish confirmed findings from items needing verification (NEEDS VERIFICATION), assign severity from exploitability, reachability, impact and context (never mechanically from a pattern, CVSS or OWASP category), do not suppress a real secret because it sits in a Development file, name workflows needing threat modeling instead of claiming the scan proves them secure, and never invent exploitability.

Verification starts by reviewing the final changed-file set and diff: confirm scope (no accidental unrelated refactoring), no generated/build artifacts, secrets or environment-specific credentials, temporary diagnostics removed only after their uniquely verified behavior is preserved; determine the affected areas before choosing checks; after fixes review the final diff again (unrelated edits, commented-out code, temporary logging, TODO/FIXME, stale temporary tests, architecture drift, unapproved drift from product inputs, stale surfaces after a settings change).

Build the affected backend solution/projects and the frontend with its configured script; a build failure means the implementation is not complete; run relevant tests (whole suite for small solutions, affected projects first for large ones) and investigate every newly failing relevant test.

For a new runnable application or substantial startup, configuration, persistence or full-stack changes verify the intended Development startup and key composition surfaces (host starts, endpoint reachable, Swagger UI loads, configuration binds, database initialization succeeds, frontend dev server starts, API base URL and CORS compatible); a successful build alone does not prove runtime composition.

For every C# file created or modified by the task remove unused or redundant using directives (including those already provided by implicit/global usings unless needed for clarity or disambiguation), verify the changed files themselves, and do not perform an unrelated repository-wide cleanup.
exceptions: Imports kept for clarity or disambiguation.

normative_action: Security-scan report shape: every report states the static-analysis limitation; severity uses the five levels Critical (sparingly) / High / Medium / Low / Info; each confirmed finding gives severity, file and location, title, evidence, why it is a risk, likely impact, smallest remediation and OWASP category when applicable; the report contains scope, limitations, a severity summary, findings and per-layer results.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-020 requires evidence-based contextual severity and WF-009 truthful status reporting; the oracle prescribes no report structure, severity scale or mandatory limitation statement.

normative_action: template-maintenance runs only when the user invokes it (disable-model-invocation; never started automatically), and maintenance keeps the always-loaded surface compact (CLAUDE.md plus the two imported decision summaries; the checker prints its estimate).
why_extra_or_uncertain: Invocation and loading-surface rules of the template; no oracle policy regulates how the instruction system is maintained.

normative_action: Instruction inventory and model integrity: the required workflow skills (project-structure, verify, code-review, build-fix, custom-settings, git-workflow, security-scan, add-dependency, architecture-decision, template-maintenance) and knowledge skills (ef-core, http-api, aspnet-error-handling, dotnet-testing, logging, httpclient-factory, configuration, dependency-injection, caching, swagger, api-versioning, health-check, docker, ci-cd, angular, modern-csharp, authentication) exist with frontmatter name equal to the directory and a description; no standalone serilog or resilience skill; agents declare name and description; CLAUDE.md is Level 0 and imports the two stratified decision summaries (1-architecture/overview.md, 3-project/decisions.md) with resolving imports; no 'Kind:' classification and no manifests, capability contracts or slots under .claude; file, skill, agent and routed-workflow references resolve; skill-private references are used only by their owning skill.
exceptions: The instruction map may list private references.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Inventory and model invariants of the L0 template; no oracle policy requires particular instruction artifacts, imports or forbids other instruction models' constructs.

normative_action: If an omitted detail must be decided and materially affects observable product behavior, propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval; defining product behavior or tunable values the product sources do not define is Reserved.

Routine internal implementation choices that do not change observable behavior do not require approval; do not ask approval for routine decisions already constrained by product sources, the approved stack, existing code or these rules.

Do not silently invent a tunable value that materially changes accepted input or observable behavior: propose it with the reason, ask for approval, record it in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md and synchronize every affected surface (custom-settings).
Never store secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers or incidental implementation constants in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.

Normative vocabulary: 'must / must not' violations are defects; a 'default' may be deviated from only with a concrete reason and the deviation must be reported; 'prefer / avoid' are guidance; 'requires approval' marks a Reserved decision.
why_extra_or_uncertain: The oracle's DEFAULT strength allows deviation for a concrete reason but requires no report of each deviation; the reporting duty and the vocabulary itself are template constructs.

normative_action: Unclear-case test: any 'yes' makes a choice Reserved — does it add, remove or replace a dependency, framework or infrastructure capability; change a project/layer/reference boundary; establish a convention other code is expected to follow; change observable behavior or a public contract; become expensive to reverse once other code depends on it?
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 requires classification but not this test; under it any unclear dependency addition or removal becomes Reserved, whereas the oracle allows dependencies with a concrete need (DEP-001) and delegates routine internal choices (GOV-005).

normative_action: Instruction precedence: engineering policy lives in the instruction system; a more volatile level may refine a more stable level but must not contradict it; when a contradiction is found it is reported instead of choosing a side.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-018 asks to raise concerns about questionable requests, including conflicts; no oracle policy defines precedence between instruction levels or requires reporting internal instruction contradictions instead of resolving them.

normative_action: Repository-wide Directory.Build.props enables nullable reference types, implicit usings and the latest analysis level for every .NET project.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-023 places shared settings in Directory.Build.props and DEP-008 fixes the platform; no oracle policy requires nullable reference types, implicit usings or the latest analyzer level.
